expect.asks_about: Which person in two-friends.jpg should receive the user's face: the bearded man on the left or the blonde woman on the right?

item.title: Which Friend Gets My Face

turns.text: Can you put my face from the park selfie onto someone in this beach photo? Just swap one face and leave everything else alone.

item.tests: Tests clarification of an ambiguous target face and preservation of the unselected person.

answer_sheet.Which person to replace: The blonde woman on the right. Leave the bearded man on the left alone.
answer_sheet.Style: Keep it looking like the original beach photo; I want to be recognisable, so my hair can come with my face.
answer_sheet.Size and platform: Keep the original wide 16:9 framing; free-tier size is fine.

must_haves: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
The bearded man on the left still looks like the same person (small drift from a redrawn photo is acceptable).
The woman on the right is recognisably the person in portrait-woman.jpg (her hair may come with the face), blended to the beach lighting and head angle.
The bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing look the same at a glance.
changed: 2026-11-01: recognisable over untouched (user decision): the hair, and on video the clothes, may come with the new person; everything else stays

turns.text: Can you put my face from this park selfie onto someone in this beach photo? I thought it would be a fun picture to have, but I’m a little worried the swap might look out of place. To explain which person I mean, it’s the blonde woman on the right in the pic of two friends, not the bearded man on the left, who should stay exactly as he is. Please use my face from the portrait selfie, and my hair can come with it so I’m recognisable, while keeping it looking like the original beach photo. The original wide 16:9 framing should stay, and free-tier size is fine. Basically, just swap that one face and leave everything else alone, with no text or other edits.
turns.agent:
I couldn’t create the swap because Magic Hour reported insufficient credits. No image was generated and no credits were spent.

The edit is set up for the free-tier size: your face and dark curly hair on the woman on the right, matched to the beach lighting, with the man and wide 16:9 framing preserved. AI editing can still introduce small unintended changes, so I can’t guarantee everything else will remain pixel-identical.

approvals.name: edit_image

args.name: Beach photo — selective face and hair swap

style.prompt: Edit the FIRST image, the beach photograph of two adult friends. Use the SECOND image, the park portrait selfie, as the identity and hair reference. Replace ONLY the blonde woman on the RIGHT's face and hair with the woman from the second image, preserving her recognizable facial features and dark curly hair. Fit the new face naturally to the beach woman's existing head angle and happy smiling expression, matching the original bright beach sunlight, shadows, skin rendering, sharpness and photographic texture. Keep her body, pose, swimsuit, and location unchanged. The bearded man on the LEFT must remain exactly as in the original: do not alter his face, hair, expression, clothes or body. Preserve the beach, ocean, sky, composition and all other details. Keep the original wide 16:9 framing, no crop, no text, no additional edits. A seamless realistic personal photo, not a collage.
